requests.title: Release Dokimos 0.11.1 with the url-input fix and register it in a new echelon-current set

options: A: merge dokimos#69, tag dokimos-v0.11.1 through Dokimos's release process, verify the published artifact, register a new echelon-current set with it and qualify it with Conditor
B: keep Dokimos 0.11.0 (INV-029's url field stays unverifiable; the catalog cannot reach GOVERNED-ACCEPTED)

requests.title: Topology for Rehearsal 010: five development lanes and one independent reviewer
requests.question: Run the build as Topology A: lanes integration, domain, persistence, ui-1 and ui-2 (each owning its implementation boundary in agent-file-ownership.json), one independent reviewer that never certifies its own work, one integration authority, one merge at a time, a bounded verification queue?
options: A: Topology A as stated (SLICE-EXECUTION-PLAN §4; schedule evidence docs/rehearsal-010-readiness/evidence/schedule/)
B: one lead agent (serial)
C: another named topology
requests.recommendation: A. It is the fastest of the five-lane assignments simulated. It does not make the full scope fit: see ODR-R10-18.
requests.rationale: The frozen schedule plans role lanes; the topology is the owner's choice (ODR-RG-05 of #101).
requests.impact: The topology sets how many slices integrate before the deadline; it does not change the scope or any gate.

requests.title: Ratify the CAT-CAUSA-INVESTIGATION successor (INV-039..044, distinct list, start and workspace routes)
requests.question: Ratify docs/rehearsal-010-readiness/proposals/causa-investigation.requirement-catalog.successor.proposed.json: every ratified requirement unchanged, INV-039..044 added (44 requirements, 277 obligations), and the screens of the investigation list, start and workspace routes? Ratification replaces the ratified catalog through tools/owner-freeze.fsx ratify rehearsal-010 and changes the scope (ODR-R10-01): 205 requirements, 890 obligations, 37 work items instead of 199, 863, 36.

B: defer the successor to a later rehearsal (Rehearsal 010 builds the ratified 38-requirement catalog)

requests.title: Approve the governed catalog-verification contract

requests.title: CF-07: how a slice gate judges bound journey assertions whose needs are not yet merged
requests.question: Under the frozen journeys rule (tools/requirements-compiler/src/Ledger.fs 391-410) every assertion bound to a slice must pass live at its merge. SL-T16 is bound to J2-08, which needs slices that depend on T16, and slices sharing J1-03/J1-06 need each other, so the approved plan can never merge T16 (execution-readiness/CROSS-AGENT-FINDINGS.md; PR #121 CF-07). How are such assertions judged?
options: A: judge a bound assertion at a slice merge only once the slices it needs are integrated; otherwise judge it at the release gate (no assertion is dropped; release still requires all)
B: rebind the cyclic assertions to the slice that completes their journey (a successor slice manifest; needs a recompile and preflight)
C: keep the rule as frozen (the approved plan deadlocks at SL-T16; Rehearsal 010 cannot complete)
requests.recommendation: A for Rehearsal 010; B as part of the v4.1.5 successor (ODR-R10-32).
requests.rationale: The deadlock is a property of the frozen bindings and gate, so only the owner can change how they are judged.
requests.impact: Without A or B no launch can complete. A keeps the published schedule (TIME-TO-WORKING-APPLICATION.md); a stricter reading moves Connect and Browse by hours (CROSS-AGENT-FINDINGS.md).

B: launch on v4.1.4 and declare in advance that EXT-DATA-013, T25 and journeys J1-06/J2-08 are expected to fail against real data
C: postpone Rehearsal 010 until A is frozen

requests.title: Competition gate: bound or remove the second browser install (L1)
requests.question: tools/r9/verification-gate.yml (governed: tools/r9/governance.json names it, r9.fsx govern copies it and check-governance requires it byte-equal) installs browsers twice on ubuntu-latest. Its browser step (line 170) is bounded to 10 minutes, but the step "Governed journeys J1-J3 and the design contract" runs a second `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit` (line 274) with no step limit, bounded only by the verify job's 40 minutes (line 49). On a stalled apt mirror, as Indy-init's own CI jobs saw three times on 2026-11-05, that install can consume the whole gate budget before the gate fails. What should the gate do?
options: A: accept the exposure; record it in docs/ci-playwright-mitigation/FINAL-REPORT.md; no workflow change

B: move the journeys' npm install and browser install into their own step with timeout-minutes: 10 (dropping it instead only if verification/journeys and the candidate's root lock resolve the same Playwright version); a governed workflow edit through r9.fsx govern, proven on a rehearsal repository before T0

C: run the verify job in the digest-pinned Playwright image used by Indy-init's adversarial jobs (#150), removing both apt-based browser installs (a small apt step for tools such as git, jq and curl remains, and the gate's other tools must be provided); a governed workflow edit through r9.fsx govern, validated on a rehearsal repository before T0
requests.recommendation: B: it bounds the stall the same way #150 bounded Indy-init's runner installs, with the smallest change to a governed file. C removes the browser installs' apt dependency but changes the gate's whole runtime this close to Nov 7.
requests.rationale: The gate decides every competition merge; an unbounded install turns a mirror stall into a 40-minute red gate instead of a 10-minute named failure.
requests.impact: A: none. B and C: the governed gate changes under tools/, so launch-preflight LP-09 needs a fresh Preflight tooling run of the new tree before launch; an agent applies the chosen option in a reviewed PR.

requests.title: Launch scope for Rehearsal 010: apply ODR-R10-19 before T0, or defer it
requests.question: ODR-R10-19 is recorded as A (APR-R10-OWNER-4: adopt the 53-item successor scope, 8baf049b...), but the lock (scope.scopeSha256 26e6ff3c...) and ODR-R10-01 launch the 37-item scope, and no agent has applied -19. The analysis recommended -19 A only together with ODR-R10-22 (speculative verification), which is recorded as A in APR-R10-OWNER-3 (authorizing the speculative gate to be built) but is not built yet; without it the split helps at fast CI and hurts at slow CI (docs/rehearsal-010-optimization/OWNER-DECISIONS-REQUIRED.md). Which scope should Rehearsal 010 launch on?
options: A: launch Rehearsal 010 on the 37-item scope ODR-R10-01 approves (26e6ff3c...); ODR-R10-19 A is not applied to Rehearsal 010 and is carried to Rehearsal 011, to be applied once the speculative gate ODR-R10-22 authorizes is built (ODR-R10-22 itself is unchanged); no lock, scope or slice file changes

B: apply ODR-R10-19 A before T0: an agent switches the lock's scope, slice manifest, work inventory and the launch docs to the successor (8baf049b...), with an independent review, and the owner then re-approves the lock's scope
requests.recommendation: A: it is the launch the lock already describes, and it keeps -19's split with the queue it was designed for.
requests.rationale: A recorded decision that is not applied must say so, so the record and the launched scope agree.
requests.impact: A: none to the launch; -19 stays recorded for Rehearsal 011. B: the scope pin moves and launch preflight LP-04 must pass on the new scope before T0.
